thesis_summary.thesis: Denison Mines Corp. (NYSE American/TSX: **DNN**) is a Canadian uranium developer and explorer incorporated in Ontario. **[Fact]** The company files annual reports on Form 40-F as a foreign private issuer; consolidated financial statements follow IFRS. **[Fact]** At December 31, 2025 the company had **901,610,950** common shares outstanding and **CAD 465.9 million** of cash and cash equivalents per XBRL (`DNN/research/evidence/sec_companyfacts.json`). **[Fact]** Reported revenue was only **CAD 4.9 million** in FY2025 while operating activities consumed **CAD 68.1 million** of cash, consistent with a pre-production developer rather than an operating miner. **[Inference]** Economic value sits in undeveloped Athabasca Basin projects (Wheeler River is referenced in reclamation disclosures) and joint-venture interests including McClean Lake and Midwest, but the Annual Information Form and MD&A that describe resources and feasibility are **incorporated by reference** in the 40-F and are **not yet downloaded** into this ticker folder.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may treat DNN as a levered bet on spot uranium when the binding variables are **permitting, project finance, and dilution**, not today's reactor demand headline. **[Fact]** FY2025 net loss was **CAD 217.3 million** while operating loss was **CAD 61.4 million**; the gap is dominated by fair-value losses on derivatives and financial instruments (CAD **111.4 million** derivative loss per XBRL), so trailing earnings are not informative. **[Inference]** Mispricing can come from **narrative_retail_flow**: uranium ETFs and AI-power thematics lift the group even when a single developer's FID timeline is unchanged. Predictive attribute: **development_milestone_gap** (equity prices embed production optionality faster than Canadian federal/provincial licensing and construction funding close).
